summary: Candidate B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload signature, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves Add behavior, and avoids unrelated retry-transport changes. Candidate A introduces a different option API, forbidden association fields, and broad retry machinery changes.
reasons: B exposes the required `Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption)` API; A instead uses `...AddFileOption`, breaking the specified convenience API and existing FilesOption pattern.
B directly reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content)`, producing the required replayable multipart body. A adds unnecessary `NewFileWithFields` machinery.
A explicitly adds association fields and option types despite the contract forbidding association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged.

A changes RawClient globally to buffer arbitrary request bodies, an unrelated retry refactor that alters Add and all other body-bearing requests. Its read failure is silently ignored after potentially consuming part of the body, creating dangerous error semantics. B keeps this behavior scoped to Upload construction and preserves Add unchanged except for documentation/tests. B validates filename and content separately and propagates multipart helper errors. Its tests verify the multipart field, filename, content, and a retry with intact multipart content.
risks_a: Upload has the wrong public signature and cannot accept existing FilesOption values.
Forbidden association APIs and multipart field support materially expand scope.

Global makeBodyReplayable changes lower-level Add behavior and unrelated requests, contrary to the preservation and scope requirements its io.ReadAll error path silently proceeds with a potentially consumed body, and it does not close the replaced body explicitly in this code path (source closure semantics may be altered). No Upload retry test or source-reader failure test is included.
risks_b: Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data check instead of routing the encoded body through `s.Add`, violating an explicit centralization requirement.
Tests omit empty-filename/nil-content validation and source-reader error propagation.
The retry test uses strings.NewReader and does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods true, so it is less directly aligned with the reported streamed-source configuration than it could be.
